doc.title: Jane Monheit interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 20, 2010

title: Musical family: son Jack, husband and father-in-law
summary: Jack's drumming and bass obsession, the family-band joke, and her father-in-law as heart of Central NY jazz.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: So I’ve read you came from a musical family. You were musical. You married into a musical family. It’s like going to definitely be in the genes of your son.

Oh yeah. He’s already got his own drumset, two years old, although he’d rather play dad’s. He’d much rather play the big drums. And my husband also has a set of electronic drums for practicing quietly and Jack will sit at the drums with the giant earphones on like engulfing his head, and play. It’s the cutest thing ever. But he’s playing real things that make sense, at two. And my husband could as well. So I’m really proud. And he loves to sing. He sings all day. And he’s obsessed with bass right now. Obsessed with bass. He turns everything into a bass.
That’s a good thing to be obsessed with. I mean for me the bass starts it all.

And my husband and I, since Jack was born, were like aww wouldn’t it be great if he’s a bass player, then it would just be like the family band. Dad on drums, Mom singing and baby bass player, grandpa playing the piano. Perfection. It’d be neat.

Oh yeah. They already love it when I do a show with my husband and father-in-law, the two of them looking exactly alike, making the same faces when they play, just like swinging their butts off together.
Your father-in-law taught me a lot.
He’s taught everybody a lot. He’s just the heart and soul of the Central NY jazz scene, and has been forever.
